ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All natural persons holding 25% or more ownership, senior managers, and the designated representative of the Taiwan investor must be screened against the PRC Political Exposed Persons (PEP) list, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic CFT watchlists. Screening must be conducted before incorporation, at bank account opening, and continuously via automated alerts every 24 hours. Negative media checks for corruption, bribery, organized crime, and sanctions evasion are mandatory. Enhanced due diligence applies where the investor is from a high-risk jurisdiction or if any UBO refuses to disclose source of funds. All screening results must be documented, escalated, and retained for a minimum of 10 years under PBOC record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Declaration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), accessed through the Integrated Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System companion portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registered name must be in simplified Chinese, following the four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry description + legal form. A corresponding English name may be listed concurrently but is not the statutory name. Pinyin or foreign letters are not permitted in the Chinese legal name except where specifically approved by SAMR. The proposed trade name must be transliterated from the vintage luxury brand into phonetically and semantically consistent Chinese characters, and must not conflict with prior registered trademarks or existing enterprise names. Homophone risk across Taiwan and mainland jurisdictions must be cleared.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written appeal with the rejecting SAMR registry within 15 working days, or apply for administrative reconsideration with the next-higher registration authority or the same-level people's government within 60 calendar days of receiving the rejection notice. If the reconsideration outcome is still adverse, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit within 15 days of the reconsideration decision. In parallel, the applicant may submit a new name application for expedited review, expressly addressing the grounds for the prior rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox addresses are not acceptable for a Chinese WFOE engaged in online luxury resale. Local SAMR registration rules require a fixed, verifiable physical address with leasing title. Tax authorities will reject a virtual office for VAT invoice issuance and E-invoice registration, and banks uniformly mandate a physical site inspection before opening a corporate account. To meet economic substance requirements, the WFOE should lease a conventional office or an enclosed shared workspace with separate office signage, maintain full-time staff, and keep records that substantiate operational presence. Using a virtual office in this industry would almost certainly trigger a revocation of registration and a bank account freeze.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood: Medium-High (roughly 45% in the first operating year for e-commerce sellers). Checklist: (1) staff present during posted business hours; (2) printed business license displayed at the registered address; (3) books, board resolutions, and UBO records available on-site; (4) VAT invoices and logistics records match physical operation; (5) access to the site is granted to inspectors; (6) no hidden subletting of the registered space. Municipal tax and SAMR officers conduct unannounced visits; failure to meet the checklist may result in fines and deregistration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of Taiwan (Company Act), as currently amended; Article 6 (incorporation upon registration), Article 18 (business scope), Articles 129-133 (articles of incorporation and share capital), Article 156 (share issuance), Article 192 (directors), Article 216 (supervisors) and Article 387 (registration with the central competent authority); Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 7 and 8 (foreign investment approval, capital remittance and approved investment scope); Commercial Registration Act; Business Tax Act; Money Laundering Control Act (relevant to high-value secondhand goods).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Section; Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) for foreign investment approval; National Taxation Bureau under the Ministry of Finance for tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form (Application for Registration of a Company) under Article 387 of the Companies Act of Taiwan, together with the Foreign Investment Approval Letter issued by the Investment Commission, MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the Companies Act of Taiwan, there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a general company limited by shares; however, the subscribed capital must be fully paid and verified by a Taiwan licensed certified public accountant before incorporation registration. No blocked escrow account rule applies for a foreign-invested company. For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the foreign shareholder must first obtain the Investment Commission, MOEA Foreign Investment Approval, then remit the approved subscribed capital into the company bank account in Taiwan. The remitted capital must be applied toward the approved investment plan, and any subsequent reduction or change in the invested capital requires separate approval or amendment filing with the Investment Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF TAIWAN VINTAGE LUXURY RESALE COMPANY LIMITED (the Company), adopted at the first meeting of the Board held at the registered office on [date], with all directors present and waiving formal notice. RESOLVED, that the Company is and shall be formed as a wholly foreign-owned company limited by shares under the Companies Act of Taiwan and the Foreign Investment Act, with the corporate name, capital and business scope as stated in the Application for Company Registration; and that the directors and officers are authorized to execute, sign, notarize and file all incorporation documents, including the Articles of Incorporation, the Company Registration Application and all related consents, before the Ministry of Economic Affairs and all other competent authorities. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company is NTD 1,000,000 divided into 100,000 ordinary shares having a par value of NTD 10 per share, and all such shares are issued at par to the sole shareholder whose subscription is hereby ratified; the initial paid-up capital of NTD 1,000,000 shall be remitted into the Company bank account in Taiwan, verified by a Taiwan certified public accountant, and remain available for the approved investment plan. RESOLVED, that the Board authorizes the opening of demand deposit, foreign currency and payment collection bank accounts with a licensed bank in Taiwan; and the Chairperson together with the Chief Financial Officer, or any two jointly designated officers, are constituted as the banking signatories for all account transactions, wires, withdrawals, deposits, payment services and escrow-related payment instructions, subject to board-approved internal controls and the Money Laundering Control Act compliance obligations. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted at [Registered Office Address, Taipei, Taiwan], and the Board authorizes the execution of a lease or use consent agreement, the retention of a local registered agent, and the filing of a registered office notice with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed for the first term: [Name] as Chairperson and Director; [Name] as Director; [Name] as Supervisor; and [Name] as General Manager, with the Chairperson and General Manager authorized to act as the statutory representatives of the Company within the ordinary course of business; if the paid-in capital and shareholding structure qualify the Company for a reduced one-director board permitted by the Companies Act for a private company, the Board shall file the registration in the permitted reduced form, provided a Supervisor is separately appointed as required by law. RESOLVED, that the Board and each officer are authorized to retain lawyers, certified public accountants, tax agents and corporate service providers, to pay all filing fees and taxes, and to take all necessary actions to complete the statutory incorporation, corporate governance registration, tax registration, bank account activation and any related business licensing for the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment Approval from Investment Commission MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taipei, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Foreign Investment Application under the Foreign Investment Act before any capital remittance to Taiwan. The application must be submitted through the MOEA Investment Commission portal and must identify the foreign corporate shareholder, the ultimate beneficial owner, the source and amount of funds, the intended ISIC 4791 online retail and secondhand luxury goods consignment scope, and the proposed Taiwan company name. Enclose the foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation, overseas board resolution, audited financial statements or bank reference, draft Articles of Incorporation, and a power of attorney in favor of the local agent. The Investment Commission will review the application for legality, national security, AML risk and capital adequacy, and issue a Foreign Investment Approval Letter that becomes the basis for bank account opening and later company registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Detailed business plan and investment plan
Notarized certificate of incorporation and good standing of the foreign shareholder
Overseas board resolution approving the Taiwan investment
Ultimate beneficial owner declaration and AML/KYC documents
Bank reference or audited financial statements evidencing source of funds
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney in favor of local service agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or queried, respond to the deficiency notice within 14 days with supplemental source-of-funds evidence and a revised investment plan; if the application is rejected, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days, or resubmit after curing the identified defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Pre-Clear Business Scope with MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), via the One-Stop Corporate Registration Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the MOEA company registration database using the proposed Chinese legal name and optional English name. File an application for approval of the company name and business scope, stating the company type as company limited by shares and the paid-up capital amount. The business scope must be expressed using the standard MOEA business scope codes applicable to ISIC 4791, such as online retail sale of secondhand or consigned vintage luxury goods. The name reservation and business scope pre-clearance are valid for six months and must be renewed if the incorporation registration is not completed before expiry. This step prevents later rejection of the registration due to identical or confusingly similar company names.
required_dossiers: Company name and business scope reservation application
Proposed Chinese and English company names
Paid-up capital amount and company type declaration
Proposed registered office administrative district
Proof of applicant identity or power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict with an existing company, submit up to three alternative names within 14 days; if the business scope is queried, amend the application to use the exact MOEA standard business scope terms and restrict the scope to ISIC 4791 online retail and consignment activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account, Remit Subscribed Capital and Obtain CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan and a Taiwan certified public accountant registered under the Financial Supervisory Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Foreign Investment Approval, the local agent shall open a temporary corporate bank account at a licensed bank in Taiwan. The foreign shareholder must remit the subscribed capital of NTD 1,000,000 from its own overseas corporate bank account, with a wire reference matching the Investment Commission approval. The bank will conduct customer due diligence, AML/CFT screening and source-of-funds review before accepting the remittance. Once the funds are credited, a Taiwan licensed certified public accountant must review the bank deposit certificate and foreign exchange transaction receipts and issue a Capital Verification Report certifying that the subscribed capital has been fully paid in cash. The Capital Verification Report is a mandatory attachment to the company incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Draft Articles of Incorporation and company name approval
Overseas bank account statements and remittance instructions
Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation and UBO declaration
Bank account application forms and board banking resolution
Power of attorney for account opening agent
Capital Verification Report issued by Taiwan CPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank holds the remittance for enhanced due diligence, provide the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, source-of-wealth declaration and structured business plan; if the bank still refuses the account, select another licensed bank and resubmit the remittance with complete remitter-beneficiary information and the Investment Commission approval reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Company Incorporation Registration with Department of Commercial Affairs MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Registration Application under Article 387 of the Companies Act through the MOEA one-stop corporate registration portal or by mail with the generated barcode. Attach the approved name reservation, Foreign Investment Approval Letter, Articles of Incorporation signed by the sole shareholder and initial directors, share subscription records, CPA Capital Verification Report, certified copies of identification documents of the initial directors and supervisor, their written consents, the registered office consent letter or landlord consent, and the power of attorney of the local filing agent. MOEA will review the legal compliance of the Articles, capital verification, statutory officers and registered office. Upon approval, MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate and the company is deemed legally incorporated, after which the tax authority will assign the uniform business tax number.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application Form
Company name and business scope approval letter
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Articles of Incorporation signed by all initial shareholders
Share subscription and capital contribution record
CPA Capital Verification Report
Written consent and identification of directors, supervisor and general manager
Registered office lease or landlord consent letter
Power of attorney for local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a deficiency notice, cure all items within 30 days; if registration is rejected, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days under the Administrative Appeal Act, or resubmit a corrected application after amending the Articles or capital verification documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax Registration, VAT Obligations and AML Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau under the Ministry of Finance; Customs Administration for import registration; Bureau of Labor Insurance for employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, register the company with the National Taxation Bureau for business tax, income tax and uniform invoice issuance. Apply for the Company Uniform Invoice Number and official seal, and register for electronic VAT filing. If the company will import vintage luxury goods for resale, register with the Customs Administration as an importer and obtain customs declaration authorizations. Because the company is engaged in online consignment and secondhand luxury goods retail, adopt a written AML program under the Money Laundering Control Act, including customer due diligence for high-value transactions, sanctions and politically exposed person screening, and record-keeping for at least five years. Also register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Company chop and uniform invoice number application
National Taxation Bureau tax registration form
Articles of Incorporation and investment approval for tax file
Customs importer registration application if importing goods
AML compliance policy and AML designated compliance officer appointment
Labor and health insurance registration forms and employment contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority queries the business scope, file a written explanation with the Company Registration Certificate and Foreign Investment Approval Letter; if a tax filing or invoice deficiency is identified, file a corrected return within 15 days and pay any assessed penalty to avoid administrative sanctions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial authority clearance is required for ISIC 4791 online retail, consignment and secondhand luxury goods resale because the entity does not operate a factory, chemical plant, assembly line or dedicated industrial warehouse under Taiwan law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no factory operation license, factory registration certificate or industrial park permit is required under the Taiwan Factory Management Act for an online retail and consignment trading company; the business is regulated only under company, tax and AML rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA tier is triggered because the operations do not involve manufacturing, chemical processing, wastewater discharge, VOC emissions or hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company performs no industrial discharge or emission activity; if the company later establishes a physical storage or fulfillment center exceeding the regulatory threshold, a separate building use, fire safety and possible local environmental review will be required at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - for a pure online retail and consignment operation, there is no mandatory civil defense fire permit, structural load inspection or factory safety clearance. However, the company must comply with the Fire Services Act and Occupational Safety and Health Act for its leased office, including maintaining portable fire extinguishers, emergency exits and basic workplace safety arrangements; if the company later opens a physical warehouse or fulfillment center, it must obtain a building use permit, fire safety equipment inspection and civil defense clearance from the local fire authority before occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; the electronic tax filing and registration portal is China Tax Service (e-tax bureau platform, accessed through the State Taxation Administration official website chinatax.gov.cn and provincial e-tax endpoints).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company established in China, the foreign sponsor first completes enterprise establishment registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), obtaining an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The USCC is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number under Chinese tax law; no separate TIN is issued. Tax registration is effected automatically through the SAMR registration data-sharing system, but the WFOE must log into the China Tax Service e-tax portal within 30 days of establishment to complete the tax information confirmation, registration of bank deposit account details, accounting software/fiscal system filing, legal representative biometric verification, and VAT taxpayer qualification election. If the projected annual taxable turnover exceeds the mandatory VAT general taxpayer threshold, the entity must apply for general VAT taxpayer status, acquire the Tax UKey fiscal control device, and enroll in the special VAT invoice issuance system. The tax registration certificate has been abolished; the USCC is the sole tax identifier for income tax, VAT, customs duty, and export tax rebate filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not operate a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election regime. A China-incorporated WFOE is automatically treated as a resident enterprise taxpayer subject to entity-level Corporate Income Tax on worldwide profits, and as a VAT taxpayer under the general or simplified collection method. The electable threshold is limited to small-scale VAT taxpayer status when annual turnover is below RMB 5,000,000, or to the simplified second-hand goods VAT collection method where applicable; no entity status classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) plus the Consumption Tax levies applicable to specified luxury goods. China uses VAT, not GST. For online consignment and secondhand luxury goods resale, the principal standard VAT rate applies to taxable sales of goods, while certain luxury items may carry additional excise/consumption tax liabilities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (annual taxable sales). Mandatory registration as a general VAT taxpayer arises once the taxpayer has an annual turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000; below this threshold, the entity may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer subject to a simplified collection rate of 1 percent or 3 percent (reduced by applicable pandemic/economic stimulus concessions).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoicing in China is governed by the State Taxation Administration's nationwide VAT invoice management system. All fapiao (tax invoices) must be issued through certified tax control equipment, including the Tax UKey and online e-tax clearance platforms. Special VAT invoices used for input tax credit, as well as ordinary VAT invoices, are transmitted in near real time to the STA and embedded with a unique encrypted anti-counterfeiting tax control code. A mandatory invoice data standardization protocol requires barcode/QR code stamping, encrypted digital signature, and daily batch reconciliation with the e-tax bureau. Fully digitalized electronic invoices (full-digital e-invoices) are accepted without OFD file format limitations. Cross-border e-commerce exports cleared under Customs supervision codes 9610 and 9710 require simultaneous synchronization of e-invoice issuance and customs declaration data, with digital ledger retention for the export tax rebate review.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: China zero-rates VAT on goods that genuinely leave the customs territory of China under an export customs declaration and are sold to a foreign buyer. For a WFOE e-commerce reseller to qualify, the sales must be supported by an export contract, a completed China Customs export declaration, the physical departure and arrival of goods evidenced by transport documents, and the repatriation of foreign exchange proceeds in accordance with State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) regulations. Alternatively, goods sold through cross-border e-commerce platforms using the 9610/9710 regulatory mode may be zero-rated provided the declared commodity, buyer, payment flow, and logistics data match to the satisfaction of customs and tax authorities. The taxpayer must be a general VAT taxpayer, maintain separate export transaction ledgers, and file the export tax rebate declaration within the statutory period. Secondhand luxury goods exported without prior input VAT credit are generally not eligible for a VAT rebate, although zero-rating still removes the 13 percent output VAT on exported secondhand goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Declaration (the export goods customs declaration form, including the scheduled departure date, destination country, commodity HS classification, customs value, and the official customs release stamp or electronic clearance date)

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export shipment from China and arrival at the destination, with issuer, vessel/flight number, port of loading, port of discharge, and cargo description consistent with the customs export declaration
Commercial Invoice and Sales Contract between the WFOE and the overseas buyer, including the exact cross-border purchase price and Incoterms

Bank Foreign Exchange Settlement/Collection Certificate proving the receipt of export-receipt foreign exchange or RMB cross-border settlement proceeds, generated by the receiving bank under SAFE trade verification procedures

Packing list, order ledger, cross-border e-commerce order initiation records, payment transaction receipts from the PSP, and the export tax rebate declaration recapitulation (often referred to as the export rebate shopping list/reconciliation sheet)
Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment confirmation evidencing the repatriation of funds within 180 days from customs clearance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: China Customs and the State Taxation Administration conduct sample-based and risk-targeted post-clearance audits of all export zero-rating and export VAT rebate claims. A false export declaration, forged bill of lading, fraudulent foreign exchange receipt, or mismatch between customs declaration and declared export revenue will void the zero-rating entitlement and trigger immediate clawback of the rebate, assessment of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest accrual, and a penalty under Article 63 of the Chinese Tax Collection and Administration Law of between 50 percent and 500 percent of the tax evaded. Concurrently, the Customs Authority may impose export smuggling penalties, revoke the issuer's Class A customs credit status, and include the enterprise record in the joint disciplinary blacklist. If the fraudulent export-rebate activity constitutes the Criminal Law offense of fraudulently obtaining export tax rebates, the responsible entity and its legal representative face criminal fines and custodial sentence risks. Re-patronage of an already-invalid exemption, failure to submit supplementary documentation, or failure to repatriate foreign exchange within 180 days also triggers automatic zero-rating revocation and retroactive interest recovery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) of the People's Republic of China, and the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC) as the dual supervisory authorities for cross-strait foreign exchange regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The composite WFOE is a PRC-incorporated wholly foreign-owned enterprise whose ultimate treasury oversight spans both mainland China and Taiwan. On the mainland, the RMB is fully convertible on the current account for trade in goods, services, and dividend remittances, but remains strictly regulated on the capital account. Inward equity capital from the Taiwanese shareholder must be registered with SAFE as foreign direct investment, held in a designated FDI foreign-exchange capital account, and settled into RMB only after the bank examines the underlying business purpose. Capital account transfers, including equity repurchases, intercompany loans, and offshore guarantees, require separate SAFE registration, filing, or approval. Profit or dividend remittances by the WFOE are treated as current-account investment income and can be paid out post-audit and post-withholding tax; the remitting bank will demand proof of tax payment, audited financial statements, board resolutions, and the FDI registration code. No automatic conversion exists for the capital account; funds received as capital cannot be used freely for equity investment, on-lending, or securities without approval. In Taiwan, the CBC operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime with no surrender duty on current-account earnings, but the Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission regulates investment flows into mainland China, and the CBC monitors large remittances. The practical effect for the WFOE treasury is that any cross-border cash movement must carry a statutory purpose code, be backed by an underlying commercial or investment contract, and be processed through SAFE/CBC-licensed banks rather than offshore payment intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: PRC (SAFE): For goods sold by the mainland WFOE, export-foreign-currency proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic foreign-exchange account generally within 90 days from the export customs declaration. There is no mandatory fixed conversion ratio; after repatriation the exporter may retain the FX in a current-account settlement account or settle it into RMB at a designated bank. Taiwan (CBC): Exporters must repatriate foreign-currency proceeds to Taiwan within 180 days of shipment, and may either retain them in a foreign-currency deposit account or convert into NT dollars at an authorized bank; the CBC may require a temporary full or partial conversion only in a balance-of-payments emergency.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Mainland China does not permit offshore EMI institutions to provide local IBANs, virtual bank accounts, or payment-as-a-bank services to a WFOE; the PBOC and SAFE require all foreign-exchange revenue and payments to be settled through licensed commercial banks and licensed cross-border payment institutions. Stripe and Escrow_Pay may be used only as merchant payment gateways that sweep funds to the WFOE's designated bank account; they cannot operate as the primary treasury cash or capital account. In Taiwan, offshore EMIs face the same treatment under the Electronic Payment Institutions Act. The overall feasibility for the WFOE is therefore Low as a stand-alone treasury rail; EMIs can add value only as customer-facing collection tools with a licensed in-country partner and full AML/KYC data transmission to the bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mainland banks require the WFOE's legal representative or a senior officer with a notarized, apostilled board resolution and original power of attorney to attend the onboarding interview in person at the branch. No pure remote or consular proxy opening is accepted for a first-time account opening. For a Taiwan-side operating account, the statutory representative or a designated Taiwan-resident director must also appear physically at the bank with corporate seals and notarised ID documents. Remote video KYC may supplement, but not replace, the physical interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value luxury consignment transactions with inconsistent provenance and recovered-value-to-volume ratio; unexplained discounts or inflated commissions between the mainland WFOE and related Taiwan counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A provenance dossier containing original purchase receipts, customs import/export declarations, VAT invoices from authorised luxury boutiques or consignors, independent condition reports from accredited auction houses or locally certified appraisers, serial-number authentication certificates, insurance policies for each item, and a margin analysis demonstrating the commercial justification for any related-party pricing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex cross-strait beneficial ownership chain featuring Taiwanese nominee directors or trust-mediated shareholders, creating uncertainty regarding the ultimate source of wealth and funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised UBO declaration prepared under PRC and Taiwan AML rules, including a full organisational chart, shareholder register for at least the last five years, certificate of incorporation and good standing, audited financial statements of each intermediate holding entity, bank reference letters, source-of-wealth documentation such as tax returns, investment sale contracts and inheritance records, and a legal opinion confirming UBO identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structuring red flag: repeated automated online sales and payouts in fractions near the RMB/NTD reporting threshold through Stripe or Escrow_Pay, with apparent splitting of a single high-value sale into multiple payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed sales ledger with unique item SKUs, customer identities, IP addresses, device fingerprints, shipping addresses, courier tracking, payment gateway transactions, settlement reports, refund records, and a reconciliation report demonstrating that each economic transaction is a bona fide retail sale to an independent end consumer; the report must enable the bank to map aggregate daily volumes and to demonstrate that no client deliberately structured to evade transaction reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering via mispriced imported and exported vintage luxury goods where the declared customs value materially differs from the market value or the same item is sold to Taiwan at a loss while related-party service fees are paid to Taiwan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party appraisals and valuation reports from internationally recognised luxury goods valuers, original brand certificates, export/import customs declarations and proof of duty payments, insurance declarations evidencing insured value, consignment contracts with a clear commission structure, freight and logistics documents, and confirmation from a registered public accountant that the transfer-pricing policy is at arm's length and the business model has economic substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwanese shareholder must first obtain regional investment approval from Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission for mainland investment, and the WFOE must complete SAFE FDI registration with its mainland bank to obtain a Foreign Exchange Business Registration (FDI) code. The injection is wired via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's FDI capital account in the named beneficiary bank; the SWIFT field 50K must identify the direct investor, field 59 must reference the FDI capital account, and the remittance information field must quote the FDI registration code, investment contract number, and the appropriate purpose code for FDI equity injection. The bank will complete currency verification and a Chinese CPA will issue a capital verification report. The funds cannot be used for non-operating items; conversion into RMB and disbursement must follow the bank's examination of supporting invoices, contracts, and the approved business scope. For the Taiwan outbound leg, the remittance is classified under the Regulations on Investment in Mainland China and must be reported to the CBC through the remitting bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational payables such as inventory purchases, appraiser fees, logistics costs, and consignor settlements, use SWIFT MT103 on a transaction-by-transaction basis when speed and traceability are required. For high-value luxury inventory purchases and larger consignments, use irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) to condition payment upon presentation of shipping, inspection, and title documents, or use Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) when counterparty risk is moderate. All disbursements must reference the underlying contract, commercial invoice, and customs entry in the payment purpose code field. For cross-border RMB settlement, route through the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) where the Taiwanese counterparty's bank participates. Aggregate settlement flows from Stripe and Escrow_Pay should be swept under a licensed cross-border merchant payment agreement into the onshore current-account settlement account so that the bank can reconcile gross transaction data with net remittances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CNY/USD deliverable forward purchase and sale contracts with SAFE-licensed onshore banks, restricted to hedging actual current-account and approved capital-account exposures.
CNY/USD cross-currency swaps for matching foreign-exchange and interest-rate risk on FDI-related loans and intercompany funding, with tenors aligned to the underlying facility.
USD/NT$ deliverable forwards executed with Taiwan authorized banks for the Taiwan-side operating entity's USD receipts and NT$ payables.
FX options on current-account flows, permissible only where the notional and tenor do not exceed the underlying exposure and the contract is entered for hedging rather than speculation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted onshore for the mainland WFOE's RMB exposures; NDFs may be considered only by the Taiwan offshore group entity through CBC-licensed banks for hedging CNY exposure that is otherwise non-deliverable in Taiwan.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual shareholders meeting record and financial statements confirmation declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce for inspection, registration evidencing and formal registry purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting may cause MOEA to order the responsible officers to convene; recalcitrant non-compliance exposes each responsible officer to administrative fines and ultimate strike-off or dissolution by the central competent authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return and final self-assessment including Alternative Minimum Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (applicable regional National Taxation Bureau)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May following the calendar tax year, or within five months after the close of an approved special fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is liable for interest on every unpaid tax amount; a late-filing surcharge accrues at 3% of the unpaid tax for each two-day delay, capped at 10%; concealed or unrealistically reported income attracts a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax plus enforced collection and asset seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic Business Tax (value-added tax) returns and annual consolidated reconciliation for online consignment and vintage luxury resale revenues
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (the tax bureau with jurisdiction over the registered business location)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by the 15th day of the month following each two-month taxable period; the November-December period return, which operates as the annual reconciliation, is due by 15 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalized administratively from NT$300 to NT$900 plus delayed-payment surcharge computed on each two-day arrear; continuous non-filing may allow the tax authority to impose surcharges up to 10%, suspend business, or revoke the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax statements, employee remuneration reconciliations, and delivery of withholding certificates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Withholding certificates delivered to payees by 31 January; annual withholding statement and electronic filing submitted by 5 February following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding agents that fail to withhold or remit remain liable for the tax; the tax authority may impose fines related to the unwithheld or underreported amount, and deliberate concealment carries enhanced administrative or criminal responsibility for the responsible officer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise operation and financial report under the foreign investment approval regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end, usually by 30 June for a calendar-year WFOE; the definitive date stated in the investment approval letter controls
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission darkens the foreign investor compliance record and may trigger remedial orders, suspension of future investment or remittance applications, or administrative fines under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register audit, shareholder and beneficial-owner confirmation, and 30-day registration of shareholding or UBO changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: External corporate secretarial auditor; documentation produced on demand to MOEA Department of Commerce and AML supervisory examiners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register audit completed at or immediately before the annual shareholders consent meeting; each share transfer, ownership change, registered-charge creation or release, and UBO update is reported within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, missing or stale statutory registers subject the company and its responsible officers to monetary penalties under the Company Act and Money Laundering Control Act; a foreign investor that fails to register share transfers may lose shareholder voting, registration-evidence, and remittance privileges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan-registered WFOE limited company must appoint an independent certified public accountant to audit its annual financial statements if any of the following statutory scale thresholds is met: (i) paid-in capital at the balance-sheet date reaches or exceeds NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 1,000,000); (ii) annual net turnover or gross sales reaches or exceeds NT$50,000,000 (approximately USD 1,700,000); or (iii) the average number of employees during the fiscal year reaches 100. An audit is also compulsory if the company is controlled by a foreign listed parent whose reporting requires Taiwan audited accounts, if the competent authority (MOEA, National Taxation Administration, Financial Supervisory Commission, or AML supervisory body) so orders because of the medium-risk-enhanced e-commerce profile, or if the company otherwise qualifies as a public or securities-issuing company regardless of size. The headcount threshold is applied against the statutory monthly/tax-reported staffing level, not merely consultant or outsourced personnel.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are prepared under the Business Entity Accounting Act, Company Act, and Taiwan-IFRS, which is the locally endorsed equivalent of IFRS implemented by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public companies under the scale thresholds may apply Taiwan-SME GAAP; in all cases the independent auditor must state the framework applied, and IFRS 15 revenue

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises (annual taxable income ≤ RMB 3 million, employee headcount ≤ 300, assets ≤ RMB 50 million) are eligible for a reduced effective tax rate: 5% for taxable income up to RMB 1 million and 10% for income between RMB 1 and 3 million. Additional R&D deduction (100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses) is available but likely irrelevant for vintage luxury resale. No specific free-zone or patent box regime applies to this entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (A-type) - Form A100000, filed through the electronic tax bureau of PRC State Taxation Administration (e-Tax@China)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional filing with annual final settlement
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly return due within 15 days after each quarter-end; annual return due before May 31 of the following calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all revenue from sale of vintage luxury goods via online platforms, net of returns and allowances. Non-resident note: Revenue from cross-border sales must be included in full; if a Taiwan-related intermediary exists, ensure no revenue is improperly diverted.
Cost of goods sold, including purchase price paid to suppliers, inbound shipping, import duties, platform fees. Adjust for intercompany purchases to arm's length.
VAT surcharge (urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge) and property/vehicle taxes.
Selling, general and administrative expenses. Disclose service fees paid to Taiwan affiliates; if such fees lack economic substance, they will be disallowed.
Operating profit plus non-operating income less non-operating expenses.
Start with total profit; add non-deductible expenses (e.g., fines, excess entertainment); subtract tax-exempt income and additional deduction; ensure transfer pricing adjustments made.
25% (or preferential 20%/10% if qualified as small low-profit enterprise).
Taxable income × applicable rate; reduce by quarterly prepayments and purchased tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: RMB 2,000 penalty per return (max RMB 20,000) or RMB 50 per day if no penalty specified; late payment: 0.05% daily surcharge (0.5‰) on overdue tax; false filing may trigger 50%-5x overdue tax penalty plus criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Related-Party Transaction Reporting Form (Form G100000, filed together with annual EIT return via e-Tax@China)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same as annual return: May 31 of next year; if contemporaneous TP documentation required, it must be prepared before the deadline and submitted within 15 days of tax authority request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all Taiwan/foreign related parties, including the WFOE's ultimate parent. Ownership percentages, tax residency, and COI (Country of Incorporation).
For each intercompany transaction: purchase of goods, sales commission, royalties, service fees, loans. Use codes.
State which method: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split. Provide justification and market data.
Fill operating margins, profit level indicators, and comparison with independent companies.
Describe personnel, assets, and functions in China that support the transaction and value creation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file related-party disclosure: RMB 500,000 fine per report; failure to furnish TP documentation within the prescribed time: RMB 100,000 to 500,000; may additionally trigger tax re-assessment and interest.
